name: Before the Dinosaurs: Life in the Ancient Seas and Swamps
description: From the soft-bodied Ediacaran to trilobites, armoured fish, coal forests and the great dying: the strange animals and plants of the Paleozoic.

checkpoints.name: Soft bodies and shells
checkpoints.note: The Ediacaran world held soft-bodied creatures. In the Cambrian, animals with hard parts appeared quickly: trilobites crawled the sea floor, and Anomalocaris and the odd Hallucigenia show how strange early animals could be.

checkpoints.name: Reefs and first plants on land
checkpoints.note: The Ordovician and Silurian seas teemed with life, and a mass extinction ended the Ordovician. Horseshoe crabs appeared, and Cooksonia and the tall Prototaxites showed life taking hold on land.

checkpoints.name: The age of fishes
checkpoints.note: The Devonian was the age of fishes: the armoured Dunkleosteus hunted, Archaeopteris formed early forests, and Tiktaalik had limb-like fins. A Late Devonian extinction hit sea life; the coelacanth lineage survived.

checkpoints.name: The coal forests
checkpoints.note: Giant club-mosses like Lepidodendron grew in swamps, and their buried remains became coal. Huge arthropods such as Arthropleura crawled the forest floor, and Pangaea began to form.

checkpoints.name: The Great Dying
checkpoints.note: In the Permian, synapsids such as Dimetrodon ruled land. The Siberian Traps erupted, and the Permian-Triassic extinction, the worst mass extinction known, wiped out most species on Earth.
